title: Minimum Total Cost to Make Arrays Unequal
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, of equal length, determine the minimum total cost of performing swaps on nums1 such that every element in nums1 is different from the corresponding element in nums2.
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, of equal length, determine the minimum total cost of performing swaps on nums1 such that every element in nums1 is different from the corresponding element in nums2. The cost of a swap is the sum of the indices of the elements swapped. Return the minimum total cost required to achieve this condition, or return -1 if it is impossible.
constraints: Swap any two positions i and j in nums1 at cost i+j.
After all swaps, nums1[i] must differ from nums2[i] at every index.
Return the minimum total cost, or -1 when impossible.
hints: Collect indexes where the arrays currently match; every such index must participate, so add their indexes to the base cost.
Count conflict values and find whether one occurs more than half the conflicts.
If dominant, add the cheapest non-conflicting indexes whose values on both arrays differ from it until the excess is balanced.
Non-dominant conflicts can be cyclically swapped among themselves; each dominant excess requires one safe outside index, and choosing them in index order minimizes added cost.
editorial: Non-dominant conflicts can be cyclically swapped among themselves; each dominant excess requires one safe outside index, and choosing them in index order minimizes added cost.

tests.explanation: Swapping positions among the five conflicts can resolve all of them with total minimum index cost ten.
Value two dominates the conflicting positions and no safe extra position exists, so the task is impossible.
